Origin: authored asset, procedurally generated by this build in a browser canvas at 1600x620, not by an image model (none exists on this machine). Brushed anodised aluminium face for the master module, the page's focal object, applied by the chassis-face utility in app/globals.css with background-size: 100% 100% and no repeat, because a single light must stay a single light.

Third generation. Generation one encoded only what a two-stop CSS gradient encodes (196 unique colours, no per-pixel information): its 'streaks' were smooth sine terms, and its noise hash multiplied past 2^53 so float64 rounding destroyed exactly the low bits the truncation read. Generation two fixed the hash with Math.imul and restored the amplitude that box-averaging divides away, but at 8.5 levels of smear the grain read as television static competing with the type. This one is the same construction at 3.4 levels.

Construction: a value-noise field (hash using Math.imul for genuine 32-bit multiplies) box-averaged along x only, radius 30 for brush lines and radius 3 for grit, so the grain is anisotropic and runs across the panel the way a brush does. Each gain is multiplied by sqrt(2r+1), because box-averaging n samples divides the deviation by sqrt(n) and omitting that is what made generation one flat. Scatter is modulated by local lighting, because brushed metal shows its grain where the key catches it and hides it in shadow. One raking key from the upper left, pow(1-(0.70nx+0.30ny), 1.4). A specular band with an actual edge: gaussian sigma 0.030 above the band centre and 0.145 below, so the highlight breaks rather than fading symmetrically. Machined edge catch on the top and left, falloff on the bottom and right. A little independent red/blue scatter, because anodising is not perfectly neutral.

Measured on the shipped file: 295 unique colours, across-brush detail 2.9 levels, along-brush 0.6, anisotropy ratio 4.8. WebP quality 90, 39.6KB. Amplitude was chosen by looking at the rendered page rather than by maximising the metric: 8.5 levels scored better on every number and looked like noise.
